https://telex.hu/belfold/2026/08/25/habl.text: Menü Kereső Ügyvédje szerint meghalt a Hableány-ügyben érintett másik ukrán kapitány, aki nem állt meg segíteni a fuldoklóknak Belföld A szerencsétlenül járt turistahajó, a Hableány roncsa a budapesti Népszigeten 2021. szeptember 22-én – Olvasói fotó / Telex Szalma Baksi Ferenc Állítsd be a Telexet megbízható forrásnak! Beállítom Ügyvédje szerint meghalt annak a hajónak a kapitánya, akit segítségnyújtás elmulasztásával vádoltak a Hableány-ügyben, írja a Blikk. Ez a hajó a Viking Idun volt, és a dél-koreai turistákat szállító Hableánynak ütköző Viking Sigyn mögött haladt. Vagyis két külön ügyről van szó. „Bemondásra nem lehet megszüntetni egy eljárást, a halál ugyanis büntethetőséget megszüntető ok. Bár a kollégám információjának hitelt érdemlősége felől nincs kétségem, a bíróságnak tudomást kell szereznie a halálról” – mondta a lapnak Borbély Zoltán, a Hableányt üzemeltető Panorama Deck Kft. ügyvédje. Azonban nagyon nehéz beszerezni a hivatalos diplomáciai iratokat a háború sújtotta Ukrajnából, ez teljesen kiszámíthatatlan folyamat. A Viking Sigyn szállodahajó 2019. május 29-én Budapesten, a Margit híd közelében nekiütközött a Hableány sétahajónak, ami ezután elsüllyedt. A sétahajón harmincöten voltak: harminchárom dél-koreai turista és a kéttagú magyar személyzet. Hét turistát sikerült kimenteni, huszonheten meghaltak. A 2023. szeptember 26-án kihirdetett elsőfokú ítélet halálos tömegszerencsétlenséget okozó vízi közlekedés gondatlan veszélyeztetésének vétsége miatt 5 év 6 hónap fogházbüntetésre, és 6 évre a vízi járművezetéstől eltiltásra ítélte a dunai hajóbaleset ügyében megvádolt ukrán hajóskapitányt. Ezt az ítéletet a Fővárosi Törvényszék hatályon kívül helyezte, és az elsőfokú bíróságot új eljárás lefolytatására utasította. A megismételt tárgyaláson a vádlott nem ismerte el bűnösségét, és nem kívánt vallomást tenni. A másik ügy a Viking Idun kapitányáé, aki szintén egy ukrán férfi, őt segítségnyújtás elmulasztásával vádolták. Kedvenceink Partnereinktől Állítsd be a Telexet megbízható forrásnak! https://wgxa.tv/news/nation-world/trump-.text: President Donald Trump has confirmed reports of an elaborate ruse for him to take a secret flight from Turkey amid threats on his life by Iran. While speaking with reporters on the tarmac after returning from the Patriot Games in Ohio on Tuesday night, Trump said the Secret Service and military wanted him on a different plane due to a threat. In his remarks, Trump ensured he was not too concerned about the threat, saying he had little choice in the matter of switching planes. The New York Times reports that Iran knew Trump's location while he stayed in Turkey for the NATO Summit, including the floor of his hotel. U.S. intelligence also had information concerning an Iranian plot to fire a surface-to-air missile at Air Force One, the outlet said, reporting intelligence officials had received a report of a person with a shoulder-fired missile in the area. On Monday, The Washington Post reported that after the NATO summit last month, Trump took a secret flight on an alternate military aircraft out of Ankara by sneaking onto a catering truck at the rear of Air Force One. They wanted me to go on a different flight, different plane. I guess there was a threat out there. I didn't really ask too much about it. I get a lot of threats," Trump said. Trump said he thinks the plane that he actually flew on was at greater risk, telling reporters it did not scare him. I don’t worry about anything, to be honest," Trump said. "Whatever it is. You know my attitude? Whatever." The Post said journalists and White House staff traveling with Trump were led to believe they were on the same flight as the president as they returned to Washington from the summit. Journalists on the flight reported being advised to keep their window shades in the press cabin closed. The reporters later asked Trump why they had to keep their shades closed, with Trump responding that they were "probably on a dangerous flight." "Well, I have a threat all the time. I'm number one on their list before you, but if I go, you go, right?" Trump said. On Wednesday, The Washington Post shared who made the catering truck switch-up with Trump. According to a U.S. official familiar with the operation, passengers on the truck included White House Deputy Chief of Staff Dan Scavino, Trump's executive assistant Natalie Harp and Director of Oval Office Operations Walt Nauta. The official told the outlet a few lower-profile aides were also present, though Cabinet members liek Secretary of State Marco Rubio were not present. On the smaller plane Trump took to Britain was Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, who the outlet said boarded the plane publicly, making him appear as the senior-most official on board. After the switch-up, Trump stopped in Britain, reboarding the baby blue Air Force One undetected. Waiting in Britain was Trump's Qatari-gifted aircraft, which the president said was sent ahead from Turkey t o Mildenhall Air Force Base so troops could see the brand-new Air Force One. “The number one priority is to use as many diversionary tactics as you possibly can so that we can put the president in that secure environment as we possibly can," former Secret Service Special Agent Richard Staropoli told The National News Desk's Ahtra Elnashar on Tuesday . According to The Washington Post, the operation "made Air Force One a 'decoy' with media and some White House staff aboard." Since Trump was secretly moved, Staropoli said it's "100% accurate" to infer the threat posed to the plane remained. “I don't think it's being overly dramatic to say, yeah, people's lives were put in danger just by being on board that aircraft," Staropoli said. Not the first 'secret trip' This isn't the first time drastic efforts have been taken to keep the president safe. In 2023, President Joe Biden's motorcade left the White House around 3:30 a.m. on a Sunday, when Biden later boarded Air Force C-32 and flew to Poland. Afterward, Biden took a secret 10-hour train ride to Kyiv, Ukraine, after Russia's invasion. The White House press pool had expected a quiet Sunday in Washington, D.C. However, two journalists traveled to Ukraine with Biden, documenting the trip. During Trump's first term, he made a secret Thanksgiving trip to Afghanistan in 2019. Officials kept a separate press pool and decoy plane to keep up the illusion that Trump remained at his Mar-a-Lago home in Florida. A separate group of reporters made the trip with Trump to the U.S. base at Bagram, where Trump served turkey to troops and met with Afghanistan's then-president Ashraf Ghani. In 2010, President Barack Obama made a nighttime visit to Afghanistan when he was said to be spending the weekend at Camp David. In 2000, President Bill Clinton secretly went from India to Pakistan. Clinton was seen talking with officials in frony of a military plane he appeared to board. Instead, he went around the front of the aircrafy to another jet parked on the tarmac. Both of the planes took off for Islamabad, including a third jet painted with the baby blue colorway of Air Force One. In this incident, Joe Lockhart, a press secretary for Clinton, said reporters knew the president was on one of the planes but "not which one." Lockhart said the pool was briefed ahead of time, and that it was made clear that "Clinton was not going to travel on the plane they were on." In 2003, when President George W. Bush made his first trip to Iraq, the news was not released until he was on the way back to the U.S. During the September 11 attacks in 2001, Bush was at an elementary school in Sarasota, Florida. After commercial flights were grounded, officials wanted him moved to an undisclosed location. The full White House traveling press pool flew with Bush to Barksdale Air Force Base in Louisiana, where officials worked to reduce the number of reporters and staff on the plane. Bush and the smaller group then flew to Nebraska's Offutt Air Force Base before returning to Washington, with the president's location remaining secret throughout the day. ______ The Associated Press contributed to this report.

https://www.politico.eu/article/emmanuel.text: PARIS — French President Emmanuel Macron said Friday he would call a Group of Seven meeting to address skyrocketing global energy prices and look at releasing strategic oil stocks. “We will have in the upcoming weeks a G7 [meeting] that will be devoted to energy issues, to increase cooperation and avoid unnecessary tensions between G7 countries and our main partners,” Macron said during a press conference. The French leader’s comments came after he chaired a rare crisis meeting at the Elysée Palace. During the meeting, French intelligence chiefs briefed political leaders and candidates in the presidential election next year about the threats posed by Russia’s war in Ukraine and the conflict in the Middle East, both of which are driving fuel prices to new highs in France. Advertisement Advertisement “The situation we face is serious. It is serious due to the international situation and the consequence of wars that we endure,” Macron said. “In this context we need to stay united.” France’s dire fiscal outlook, which has prompted the government to pursue a €54 billion budget squeeze next year , will make it difficult for the state to massively subsidize increasingly expensive energy bills. Macron told reporters, however, that the government was working on targeted assistance proposals. Macron also said he was seeking to firm up French access to oil and gas supplies during recent meetings with leaders from Saudi Arabia, Iraq, Qatar and the United Arab Emirates. He added that he’d discuss France’s trade in petroleum products and liquefied natural gas with Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney when the two meet on Sunday . The president said France was stepping up efforts to protect critical infrastructure and defense production sites amid the uptick in cyberattacks and the intensified threat of so-called hybrid attacks from Russia, including recent ones on a Ukrainian passenger train and at Leipzig airport in Germany. Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk warned Thursday that Russia was planning to target Ukraine’s European allies using drones or rockets. Among those in attendance were center-right former Prime Minister Edouard Philippe, centrist Gabriel Attal, conservative candidate Bruno Retailleau, center-left Raphaël Glucksmann, Greens leader Marine Tondelier and Socialist Party chief Olivier Faure. Far-right presidential candidate Marine Le Pen, who has a commanding lead in the polls, was represented by her party’s president, Jordan Bardella, while far-left hopeful Jean-Luc Mélenchon was represented by a high-ranking lawmaker from his party, Manuel Bompard. The politicians who spoke to reporters after the meeting acknowledged the gravity of what had been discussed. Guillaume Lacroix, the head of a small left-wing party, wrote online that the stakes of the three-hour briefing had made his head spin. Advertisement Advertisement “In my 50 years, I have rarely felt such a sense of vertigo,” he said. “Vertigo at the gravity of the situations in the Middle East and Ukraine, and at the predatory madness driving the world toward chaos.” But Macron’s opponents criticized him for failing to present solutions during the forum to bring down energy prices. “The question of purchasing power was swept aside,” said Bardella. Retailleau, who leads the conservative party Les Républicains, said he had suggested “a number of proposals” during the meeting. Advertisement Advertisement

https://www.theguardian.com/politics/202.text: A woman walks past a polling station in Primrose Hill, in the constituency of Holborn and St Pancras, on Thursday. Photograph: Leon Neal/Getty Images View image in fullscreen A woman walks past a polling station in Primrose Hill, in the constituency of Holborn and St Pancras, on Thursday. Photograph: Leon Neal/Getty Images Holborn and St Pancras byelection Polls close in Holborn and St Pancras byelection as Labour hopes to retain seat Contest seen as test of Andy Burnham’s ability to unite Labour voters amid threat from Green party’s Zack Polanski Aletha Adu and Nadeem Badshah Thu 8 Oct 2026 18.43 EDT First published on Thu 8 Oct 2026 17.00 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google Polls have closed in the Holborn and St Pancras byelection , a contest seen as a test of whether Andy Burnham can unite Labour’s voters or whether Zack Polanski can peel off support from the party’s progressive flank. Labour is seeking to retain Keir Starmer’s former north London seat, where he won a majority of more than 11,000 votes in the 2024 general election . The byelection is seen as a measure of the political landscape under Burnham, almost three months into his premiership. It is a significant first electoral test for Burnham, who succeeded Starmer in July , as part of a wider battle for younger leftwing voters who became disillusioned with the party under Starmer’s leadership over issues such as housing, the climate crisis and the war in Gaza. Polanski has sought to run an energetic campaign involving thousands of activists, leaving the Green party conference early after his speech in an attempt to prove he and the Greens are a serious rival to Labour, despite the latest polling. View image in fullscreen Zack Polanski, seen campaigning in London last month, said he did not believe a defeat in the byelection would undermine his leadership of the Green party. Photograph: Andy Hall/The Guardian The Greens are hoping to reproduce their byelection victory in Gorton and Denton in February where they overturned a Labour majority. However, the political landscape has shifted since then. Shortly after their byelection win in Greater Manchester, YouGov polling put the Greens on 21%, a few points ahead of Labour . But the latest YouGov survey put the Greens 16 points behind Burnham’s Labour, which was on 27%. The poll came as Burnham proposed a more ambitious pitch to progressives at his first Labour conference as prime minister. Holborn and St Pancras has a large number of students, younger voters and renters, with almost half of residents aged between 18 and 34, while about 45% were born overseas. Polanski has argued that electing him would increase pressure on Labour to deliver more radical policies, including stronger rent controls, greater action on the climate crisis and public ownership of Thames Water. But the leader of the Greens has faced questions about his own authority and was accused of being unable to articulate his thoughts on motions that became policies at his party’s conference. In an interview with the Guardian last Friday , Polanski described the contest as “probably 50/50” and that it was “really on a knife-edge” while also insisting his leadership did not depend on victory. View image in fullscreen Labour’s candidate Sagal Abdi-Wali is hoping to become Keir Starmer’s successor as the MP for Holborn and St Pancras. Photograph: Antonio Olmos/The Guardian Asked whether losing the byelection would undermine his position, Polanski said: “It doesn’t depend on it whatsoever.” Senior Green figures privately fear a defeat could severely damage his reputation amid concerns the party’s increase in members has not translated into an advantage in campaigning. Labour has fielded Sagal Abdi-Wali , the 42-year-old leader of Camden council who arrived in Britain as a child refugee after her family fled civil war in Somalia. She has emphasised her longstanding connections to the area, presenting herself as locally rooted, and with experience of community work, homelessness and housing policy. The closing days of the byelection campaign were overshadowed by a row within the Green party after members voted at their conference to adopt a policy equating Zionism with racism , which passed by 1,022 votes to 813 despite opposition from four of the party’s five MPs. Polanski, who is Jewish, left the conference early to campaign in north London and did not participate in the vote. As polls closed on Thursday, Burnham said the Green party’s Zionism motion was “completely wrong”. Speaking to journalists on a trip to Berlin, the prime minister said it showed “terrible judgment on behalf of the Green party” and “shouldn’t be supported in any way, shape or form”. The Labour leader called on Polanski “to say that it will be reversed and it won’t be Green party policy”, adding: “In my view, all political parties in the UK should do everything they can to support the two-state solution between Israel and Palestine.” The byelection result may provide some insight into whether Burnham’s recovery in national support is translating into Labour’s inner-city strongholds, and into whether the Greens can continue to attract younger and progressive voters. It will also offer a test of Polanski’s argument that the Greens can put pressure on the government from the left, even as Labour seeks to reclaim voters it lost under Starmer. Polls closed at 10pm on Thursday and the result is likely to be announced between 2:30am and 4am on Friday. https://www.forbes.ro/dan-andrei-muraru-.text: The Embassy of Romania in Washington is opening up to Romanian companies the network of contacts it has built across all 50 US states, from governors and local authorities to chambers of commerce and investors. The offer was made by Ambassador Dan-Andrei Muraru at the opening of Forbes România Business Bridges 2026, the event organized by Forbes Romania at Forbes on Fifth in New York. "This is our offer to you. Please use us. Come to us. We can share with you everything we have, from contacts to the experience we have gained in the past years," the ambassador told the business leaders in the room. At stake is an imbalance the diplomat named directly. The United States is Romania's fourth-largest foreign investor and its largest from outside the European Union, with a stock of direct investment of more than 9 billion, roughly 7% of Romania's total foreign direct investment. In the opposite direction, the presence of Romanian companies across the Atlantic remains modest. "The investment footprint of Romanian companies in the United States remains below its potential. We should therefore aim to see more Romanian companies become not only exporters, but investors, employers and long-term business partners here in the States," Muraru said. The trade relationship is not starting from zero. "In 2025, our trade reached approximately 9.4 billion, with exports of goods and services of 6.4 billion, including more than 4 billion in services, 60% of which came from the IT&C sector," the ambassador noted. The problem, in his view, is that many Romanian entrepreneurs treat America as a single market. "The United States is a market of 50 states, each with its own regulatory framework, tax provisions, incentives and business environment. What works in New York may not necessarily work in Texas, Florida, Ohio, Virginia or Arizona," Muraru explained. This observation gave rise to "50 States, One Community," the initiative through which the ambassador set out to visit every US state. Its stated goal is a structured dialogue with local business communities, giving Romanian companies more than general market information. "Companies need access to legal, financial, tax, investment and local market expertise, as well as the right connections. This is where the Romanian Embassy and its economic diplomacy network can make a practical contribution," the diplomat stressed. The sectors where he sees the greatest opportunities are energy, artificial intelligence, cybersecurity, advanced manufacturing, defense, critical minerals, infrastructure and logistics. The equation he proposes is one of complementarity: Romania brings industrial capabilities, a skilled workforce, strategic resources and access to the European market, while the United States offers capital, technology, industrial expertise and access to global markets. The long-term goal is for the Romanian-American relationship to move beyond trade and individual projects towards a strategic business partnership. The state's role has clear limits, however, the ambassador acknowledged: governments create the framework, diplomacy opens doors, but it is entrepreneurs who turn opportunities into businesses. "My message to Romanian companies is simple: the American market is open to opportunity, but entering it successfully requires preparation, local knowledge, the right partners and a long-term commitment. The Romanian Embassy is here, ready to support companies willing to take that step," Dan-Andrei Muraru concluded.
